  PROBLEM: Reviewed guard symlinks can point outside the reviewed `.claude/` tree, allowing the sync to compare against and copy unreviewed twin or out-of-tree content to consumers.
  WHY: `-f`, `cmp`, and `cp` follow symlinks without checking their resolved targets; reviewers rated this BLOCKER or MAJOR, with BLOCKER the highest severity.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Enforce that a reviewed guard symlink resolves within the owner-reviewed `.claude/` tree, never to its twin or another out-of-tree path.
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/update_workflows.yml`, first-pass guard arm and second-pass reviewed-tree pass
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `.github/workflows/update_workflows.yml` uses `[ -f ]`, `cmp`, and `cp` without checking the resolved target boundary; `agents.md` documents symlinks resolving to regular files without an in-tree constraint.

- requirement: Add a behavioral test for a reviewed guard symlink targeting `workflow-templates/.claude/` or another path outside the reviewed `.claude/` tree, and assert the out-of-tree content is not installed.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py`, alongside `test_claude_sync_installs_a_symlinked_reviewed_guard_without_a_regular_twin`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `test_claude_sync_installs_a_symlinked_reviewed_guard_without_a_regular_twin` tests only an in-tree target (`hooks/linked.py` -> `real.py`); no fixture exercises a target in `workflow-templates/.claude/` or elsewhere outside the reviewed tree.

- requirement: Document that reviewed guard symlinks must resolve within the owner-reviewed `.claude/` tree.
  expected_change_site: `agents.md`, `README.md`, and `changelog.d/5607-consumer-guard-source.md`
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `agents.md` describes symlinks resolving to regular files without an in-tree constraint; `README.md` and `changelog.d/5607-consumer-guard-source.md` likewise omit the constraint.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml | Lines 259-260, 267, 288 (first pass guard arm) and lines 315, 325 (second pass) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `[ -f ]`, `cmp`, and `cp` follow symlinks; when a reviewed guard symlink targets the twin tree, the comparison sees the same file at both paths and the copy installs twin content without a warning or fresh owner review.
  WHY: A future owner-approved symlink can let all subsequent twin changes flow to consumers silently.

Requirement: The PR description states "A guard file is therefore copied from the same commit's .claude/ tree, never from its twin." The agents.md bullet (line 1340) documents the symlink case as "a symlink there is installed as its target's content when it resolves to a regular file, and installs nothing otherwise" — with no constraint that the resolved target must live inside the reviewed `.claude/` tree. The symlink-dereference path at lines 259-260 (`-f`), 267 (`cmp`), 288 (`cp`), 315 (`-f`), and 325 (`cp`) follows any regular-file target, including one in the twin tree.
Expected change site: `.github/workflows/update_workflows.yml`, the first-pass guard arm (lines 259-260) and second-pass guard block (line 315): either reject symlinks entirely with `[ -L "${claude_source_path}" ]` before `-f`, or resolve the realpath and verify it starts with `${CLAUDE_REVIEWED_DIR}/`. And `changelog.d/5607-consumer-guard-source.md`, `agents.md` lines 1327-1347, and `README.md` lines 1061-1065: the documented symlink rule should state the in-tree-only constraint.
Evidence of absence: The diff adds `-type l` to the reviewed-tree `find` (line 329) and the test `test_claude_sync_installs_a_symlinked_reviewed_guard_without_a_regular_twin` exercises only in-tree targets (`hooks/linked.py` → `real.py` in the same reviewed tree). No check verifies the resolved path stays inside `${CLAUDE_REVIEWED_DIR}`. No test fixture has a reviewed guard symlink pointing to the twin tree (`../workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/x.py`) or to an arbitrary path. The agents.md symlink description at line 1340-1341 says only "when it resolves to a regular file" with no boundary constraint. The README note at line 1061-1065 and the changelog fragment both omit the constraint.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml | lines 257-279 and 304-330 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Reviewed guard symlinks are followed by file checks, comparisons, and copy operations without verifying their resolved targets remain within the reviewed `.claude/` directory.
  WHY: A symlink to the twin can make `cmp` report equality and cause unreviewed twin content to be copied to consumers; the second pass also copies symlink targets outside `.claude/`.

Requirement: A guard file is therefore copied from the same commit's `.claude/` tree, never from its twin (PR description, line 4; agents.md: "Consumers get guard files from `.claude/`, not the twin"). The owner-reviewed `.claude/` tree must be authoritative and cannot be bypassed via symlinks pointing back to the unreviewed twin tree.
Expected change site: .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml in the "Sync .claude/ assets from upstream" step (first-pass guard arm lines 257-279 and second-pass lines 304-330).
Evidence of absence: The step uses [ -f ], cmp -s, and cp without enforcing that a reviewed guard symlink's canonical target is contained strictly within CLAUDE_REVIEWED_DIR and does not reference CLAUDE_UPSTREAM_DIR or other paths outside the reviewed tree.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Requirement: Behavioral tests must verify that guard assets cannot bypass owner review by symlinking to workflow-templates/.claude/ or outside the reviewed .claude/ tree.
Expected change site: tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py, in or alongside test_claude_sync_installs_a_symlinked_reviewed_guard_without_a_regular_twin.
Evidence of absence: test_claude_sync_installs_a_symlinked_reviewed_guard_without_a_regular_twin only tests in-tree symlink targets (hooks/linked.py -> real.py). There is no test fixture exercising a reviewed guard symlink targeting workflow-templates/.claude/ or outside .claude/ to assert that unreviewed twin or out-of-tree content is rejected and not installed.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Requirement: agents.md and README.md must document the in-tree restriction for reviewed guard symlinks so that future maintainers do not introduce twin-pointing or out-of-tree symlinks.
Expected change site: agents.md lines 1324-1350 and README.md lines 1058-1068.
Evidence of absence: agents.md currently states only "a symlink there is installed as its target's content when it resolves to a regular file, and installs nothing otherwise" without specifying that the target must resolve within the reviewed .claude/ tree. README.md and changelog.d/5607-consumer-guard-source.md likewise omit the in-tree constraint.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml | lines 260, 267, 274, 288 (first-pass guard arm); lines 315, 325 (second-pass reviewed-tree pass) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The reviewed-tree guard arms follow symlinks without verifying that resolved targets live inside `${CLAUDE_REVIEWED_DIR}`.
  WHY: A symlink to the twin can pass the file check, compare as the same blob, and be dereferenced by `cp`, installing twin content on consumer syncs without a warning.

Requirement: A behavioural test that exercises a reviewed guard symlink whose target is OUTSIDE the reviewed `.claude/` tree (e.g. into `workflow-templates/.claude/`, a sibling tree, or an arbitrary filesystem path) and asserts the consumer does not receive that out-of-tree content as a guard.
Expected change site: tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py, sibling to test_claude_sync_installs_a_symlinked_reviewed_guard_without_a_regular_twin (lines 576-607)
Evidence of absence: The shipped test creates only in-tree targets (`hooks/linked.py` -> `real.py`, where `real.py` exists at `hooks/real.py` in the same reviewed tree). No fixture exercises a symlink whose target resolves outside `${CLAUDE_REVIEWED_DIR}`, so the BLOCKER finding above has no automated witness — the suite passes today on the vulnerable code.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Requirement: agents.md, README.md, and the changelog fragment describe the in-tree constraint so future maintainers do not add reviewed guard symlinks that bypass the contract.
Expected change site: agents.md lines 1324-1350 (the "Consumers get guard files from `.claude/`, not the twin" bullet); README.md lines 1058-1068 (the hooks note); changelog.d/5607-consumer-guard-source.md
Evidence of absence: agents.md says "a symlink there is installed as its target's content when it resolves to a regular file, and installs nothing otherwise", with no caveat that the target must live inside the reviewed `.claude/` tree. README.md says "a guard with no twin is installed from `.claude/` only where the consumer lacks it", also without the in-tree constraint. The changelog fragment likewise does not mention the constraint.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
